item.title: Bin Snooper 1.7.13
item.description: Shares anonymous usage counts once a week (days used, how many times each job ran, how many failed and the kind of error). Never your name, licence, Mac, files or anything you work on. Turn it off in Something not right? > Share anonymous usage counts.

item.title: Bin Snooper 1.7.12
item.description: Send logs now sends the zip to Pete itself, attached, with a note of what happened - no email app needed. If it can't, the email opens and Finder comes to the front with the zip ready to drag on.

item.title: Bin Snooper 1.7.10
item.description: The Dock icon shows how many possible crash locks there are, with a soft sound when a new one turns up (Settings: switch the sound off).

item.title: Bin Snooper 1.7.9
item.description: Send logs is easier: pick Gmail, Outlook, the Mail app or just the zip. Gmail and Outlook open in your browser with the email filled in, so nothing needs setting up on the Mac. Your choice is remembered for the Send logs buttons on error messages.

item.title: Bin Snooper 1.7.8
item.description: The opening wallet's name is bigger and sized to the window.

item.title: Bin Snooper 1.7.7
item.description: The opening wallet shows the name on two lines, a bit bigger.

item.title: Bin Snooper 1.7.6
item.description: When a project's drive comes back under another name, the note says so plainly. Problems listed in Settings have a Send logs button next to them.

item.title: Bin Snooper 1.7.5
item.description: New: a 'Check my setup' button in Settings that ticks off the licence, macOS, internet, disk space and your watched projects, and says how to fix anything missing. It opens by itself the first time. After each update you'll see a short note like this one. If a drive comes back as FAL_PRJ-1, Bin Snooper now says so plainly.

item.title: Bin Snooper 1.7.4
item.description: Updates can now bring newer helper tools (Python, ffmpeg). Logs go to apps@drpob.com.
